---
name: hub-experiment-evaluation
description: Plan and document repeatable software, ML, research, and agent-harness experiments (EXP) and cross-run/design comparisons (EVAL). Use for benchmarks, ablations, model or prompt comparisons, performance studies, experimental runs, and evidence for choosing between design versions.
---

# Experiment & Evaluation

**Scope:** Experiment plans, reproducible executions, measurements, and comparative findings. For design/ADR changes use `hub-design-decision-management`; for docs indexes and audits use `hub-docs-governance`.

## Records and storage

- `docs/experiments/EXP-0001-slug/plan.md`: question, falsifiable hypothesis, baselines, protocol, metrics and stopping criteria.
- `docs/experiments/EXP-0001-slug/results.md`: actual runs, measurements, failures, uncertainty, limits and conclusion.
- `docs/evaluations/EVAL-0001-slug.md`: synthesis comparing multiple experiments, design versions, datasets, or methods against decision criteria.
- **Do not copy every run into Markdown.** Use MLflow, W&B, DVC, or a durable artifact store to hold parameters, logs, raw metrics, models and traces. Reference tracker URLs/run IDs and dataset versions.

## Procedure

1. Read existing EXP/EVAL documents, relevant `DES-xxxx@vN`/RFC/ADR, code/tests, tracker conventions, and data provenance.
2. Allocate a unique `EXP-xxxx` ID and **write a plan before interpreting outcomes**. State a falsifiable question, baseline, intervention/variant, fixed controls, success threshold, secondary trade-offs and failure conditions.
3. Specify comparable datasets/tasks, sampling, splits, random seeds, versioned configuration, evaluation method and known confounders. Avoid leakage and cherry-picked examples.
4. For reproducibility capture: **Git commit, design ID/version, environment, configuration hash, dataset/benchmark version, random seeds, run IDs, artifact URIs**. For agents also log provider/model version, prompt/hash, tool set/permissions, harness version, tool traces and grader version.
5. Execute **only when requested and possible**; otherwise leave status `planned`. Log all runs, including failures, negative and inconclusive outcomes. Never fabricate results.
6. Write `results.md`: run table or tracker links, effect sizes, dispersion/uncertainty, failure analysis, limitations, and supported/not-supported/inconclusive conclusion.
7. For cross-study comparisons write `EVAL-xxxx`, state comparability and recommendation confidence. Link the EVAL back to DES/RFC/ADR without automatically adopting a design.
8. Set statuses based on evidence (`planned`, `running`, `completed`, `aborted`; EVAL `draft`/`final`) and update `docs/README.md`.

## Templates

### EXP plan

```markdown
---
id: EXP-0001
title: Sequential versus parallel execution
status: planned
created: YYYY-MM-DD
updated: YYYY-MM-DD
related: [DES-0001@v1, DES-0001@v2]
---
# EXP-0001 — Sequential versus parallel execution
## Question and falsifiable hypothesis
## Baseline / treatment / controls
## Data, sampling, splits and protocol
## Versions: commit, designs, models, prompts, tools, config, seeds
## Primary and secondary metrics / success thresholds
## Risks, confounders and stopping criteria
## Run tracker, artifacts and reproduction instructions
```

### EXP results

```markdown
# EXP-0001 — Results
- Status / run dates:
- Code / dataset / config versions:
- Tracker URL, run IDs and artifact links:

| Variant | Valid runs | Primary metric | Latency | Cost |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Baseline | … | … | … | … |
| Treatment | … | … | … | … |

## Uncertainty, failure cases and caveats
## Interpretation and conclusion (supported / unsupported / inconclusive)
## Reproduction links and next steps
```

### EVAL comparison

```markdown
---
id: EVAL-0001
title: Harness execution comparison
status: draft
created: YYYY-MM-DD
updated: YYYY-MM-DD
related: [EXP-0001, DES-0001@v1, DES-0001@v2]
---
# EVAL-0001 — Harness execution comparison
## Decision question and comparison criteria
## Evidence sources and comparable runs
## Results and uncertainty
## Trade-offs, failures and limitations
## Recommendation (confidence + conditions)
## Source run IDs, artifacts and related ADR
```

## Quality gates

- No invented sample sizes, numbers, runs, outcomes or statistically unsupported causal claims.
- Never mark `completed` without observable result evidence; mark aborted runs with reasons.
- Preserve negative results; don't compare incompatible evaluations as if controlled.
- `EXP-xxxx` identifies a research question/protocol, not a single run; actual tracker run IDs are separate.
